note.text: Soil erosion is detachment and movement of soil by water, wind or other agents. It differs from weathering, which breaks down material in place. Raindrop impact can detach exposed particles; runoff transports them. Sheet wash removes a thin surface layer, while concentrated flow can form rills and gullies. Deposition occurs when transported material settles. Slope, cover, rainfall intensity, soil condition and land use interact. Removing topsoil can reduce rooting depth and nutrient stores and send sediment into watercourses.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish detachment transport and deposition and explain how cover and runoff influence loss. Builds on: soil properties and the profile. Leads to: choosing measures that address erosion processes.

sections.heading: Explain the geography

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: An invented school comparison uses equal areas and equal rainfall to compare covered and bare soil. A measured difference supports a conclusion about those models under those conditions; it does not establish a national erosion rate. On western highland slopes, exposed ground and concentrated runoff help explain risk, while vegetation and stable structure can reduce it. Wind erosion is also relevant where dry loose surfaces lack protection.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Trace source, pathway and deposit. Distinguish evidence of detachment from evidence of accumulated sediment. Compare like conditions before attributing all differences to cover. Do not inspect active gullies or enter floodwater; the lesson uses drawings and supplied measurements.

cards.idea: Explain how the process produces the stated effect.
example: Detachment is the start of removal, distinct from later transport and deposition.
Transport distinguishes removal by erosion from weathering in place.
Flow can converge and increase local erosive action.
Deposition shows accumulation but requires more evidence to trace all sources and quantities.
